title: Masa para los Pasteles de Hoja (Dough for Puff Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolks, butter, and flour.
steps: Take one pound of butter and one pound of flour and four egg yolks. Take half of the flour and form a small mound, place the yolks in the middle; a little water and a small piece of butter that is not salted, join all this together and make a very soft dough.
Beat it well with the hand until it becomes very smooth. Add a little flour, knead well and roll it out, fold in three times.

title: Mayonesa (Mayonnaise)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, vinegar, and oil.

Beat well for about three hours, adding two tablespoons of oil from time to time until you calculate about half a bottle of regular size

Stir well and add the necessary salt
Arrange a dish with lettuce leaves, tender radishes and pieces of celery opened in water

description: Prepared with rice, watermelon, and zucchini.
steps: Choose a watermelon according to the number of diners.
Cut off the top as a lid and carefully hollow it out, removing the flesh in presentable pieces to serve as an appetizer at the beginning of the meal.
Continue cleaning the inside of all its flesh until only the rind remains, with the interior well smoothed, resulting in a cavity shaped like a bowl.
Inside, place pre-fried oil, small pieces of zucchini, chicken, fish or meat that have been previously seasoned.
Season well; add very finely cut peppers and tomatoes.
Fill the watermelon with water to two or three fingers below its edges.
Add rice in an amount equal to one third of the volume of what is contained in it.
Cover with the lid placed upside down, and with a piece of strong canvas, tie and secure the watermelon well so that the lid does not shift.
Dig a hole in the ground, bury the watermelon, and cover it with some sand.
Then spread quicklime on top to form a mound, and extinguish it with water.
After three quarters of an hour, remove the watermelon and serve this perfectly cooked and flavorful rice, made without fire and without a vessel.

title: Bacalao á la Provenzal - Brandado (Salt Cod Provençal Style - Brandade)
description: Prepared with salt, onion, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: about two pounds of well-desalted salt cod from the thickest part

steps: Take about two pounds of well-desalted salt cod, but making sure it is from the thickest part; cut it into square pieces and put it in a sufficient quantity of cold water so that it cooks on low heat, and when it is about to come to a boil, set it aside and cover it with its lid, leaving it in this condition for about ten minutes
After which drain it through a sieve, and then through cloth or canvas so that no moisture remains; carefully remove the bones, leaving the skins
Fry in a casserole in very fine oil a chopped onion with a bay leaf, then putting the cod inside and stirring it strongly with the spatula until it becomes a paste
During this work put in some tablespoons of very fine oil, letting it fall very slowly, and at the same time some drops of lemon juice
By force of work and with the help of the oil and lemon, the cod acquires a whiteness and surprising elasticity, thus transforming itself into a healthy and appetizing food

title: Becacines en Salmorejo (Woodcock in Sauce)
description: A sauce made with woodcock, lemons, and lemon.

ingredients.name: zest of one lemon, grated to powder
two teaspoons of good French mustard
half a glass of white wine

steps: Roast the two woodcock on the spit at medium doneness after cleaning them very well on the outside, since it is known that inside, like shells and snails, this animal is not emptied.

When the woodcock are half-roasted, divide them according to all the good rules of the art of carving, and then cut the wings, legs, stomach, and tail into two pieces, placing the pieces on a platter.

On the silver plate (or moirez or alfenide) in which the dissection has been made, crush and squash the livers, intestines, and all the giblets of the birds, squeezing the juice of four well-fleshy lemons and the grated zest of a single lemon over them.
Place the cuts of the woodcock on top, seasoning them with salt, pepper, nutmeg, and two teaspoons of good French mustard, adding half a glass of white wine.
Place the plate on a spirit lamp (called infierno), and stir constantly with a silver fork so that during this last point of cooking the sauce coats well and the pieces do not stick.

Take great care that everything cooks inside without boiling, and when you see that this moment is about to arrive, add a few drops of oil and remove the plate from the flame of the spirit lamp, and begin again until the operation is complete.
Eat this salmorejo very hot, with a fork and not with the hand, as with all birds, for the risk of devouring your fingers while sucking the sauce.

title: Biftec à l'Anglaise (English-Style Beefsteak)
description: Prepared with fat, beef, and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: one whole sirloin, cleaned of fat, skin, and tendons

a few drops of lemon juice

steps: From a whole sirloin cleaned of fat, skin, and small tendons, cut twelve regular beefsteaks, neither very thick nor very thin, cutting the meat against the grain with a long, sharp knife blade.
Profile each beefsteak in a round shape by trimming the edges, and then on the cutting board, beat both sides with a heavy, long boxwood mallet.
Sprinkle salt on both faces of the beefsteak.
Melt 125 grams of beef butter over low heat in a saucepan for six regular-sized beefsteaks, and while the butter is liquid but not very hot, dip the beefsteaks in it on both sides using a fork.
Then place all of them together on the grill over coals that should not be too lively nor half-extinguished.
When the beefsteaks have been well seized by the fire and have taken on color without being burned, making the cooking give firmness to their meat, then remove them from the fire.

Once the beefsteaks are done, place them on a round platter in the form of a crown, and in the center place, for six beefsteaks, 125 grams of very fresh butter, kneaded with salt, pepper, and very finely chopped parsley, seasoned with a few drops of lemon juice.
The beefsteaks are served with the maitre d'hôtel sauce as described.
The platter in which the dish is served must be very hot beforehand, submerged in boiling water, so that the beef butter melts and remains fluid with the heat of the meat.

The beefsteaks may be served English-style with fried potatoes covering the plate literally, or with potatoes cooked in steam and cut into slices, which placed in the center will take on the seasoning of the beefsteak.

title: Buñuelos (Spanish Fritters)
description: Prepared with fat, eggs, and flour.
steps: Crack one egg into a saucepan and stir with a spoon; when well mixed, add two more eggs, one after the other; mix well, and if the paste is too hard, add half an egg or a whole egg as needed.
To test the consistency of the paste, take a quantity the size of an egg on a spoon and let it drip. It should not spread nor remain stuck to the spoon, but should be pulled down by its own weight.

When the dough is finished, dust the table with flour, and place a quarter of the dough on it; dust this also with flour so it does not stick to the table or hands, and cut into pieces to form balls of two and a half centimeters, which are lined up on strips of paper four centimeters wide, which will have been lightly greased with frying fat.

Put three pounds of frying fat in a frying pan, which is tested by frying a small piece of bread that should barely quiver; place the pan beside the stove; dip the paper strip in the frying fat and remove when the fritters have separated; move with a skimmer and increase the heat of the frying fat by gradually moving the pan to the fire until it is completely over the stove.
When the fritters are golden and dry, drain them on a clean kitchen cloth, dust with sugar and arrange in a pyramid on a platter over a folded napkin.

Beat egg whites until they resemble meringue and mix with the batter

title: Café Según lo Hacen en los Cafés (Coffee as Made in Cafés)
description: Prepared with ground coffee, fish, and water.

ingredients.name: 200 grams of roasted and ground coffee of the day

steps: Fill two-thirds of a large coffeepot with water and the rest with residue from previously made coffee.

Remove and discard the old coffee residue from the coffeepot.
Clean the coffeepot and add 200 grams of roasted and ground coffee of the day for each fifteen cups of prepared water.
Dissolve a few grams of fish glue in the water and add 50 grams of chicory.
Stir well with a spatula and place the vessel over high heat, covered hermetically.
As soon as it has boiled for two or three seconds only, remove from the fire and let the coffee clear, stirring well.
Decant carefully by pouring in a thin stream, transferring it to an earthenware container that is kept from that moment in a bain-marie, taking care that it does not boil.

title: Callos á la Madrileña (Madrid-Style Tripe)
description: Prepared with tripe, garlic, and carrots.

ingredients.name: Five pounds of tripe for ten persons
Three quarters of a pound of lard
Three quarters of a pound of lean, well-cured ham, cut into dice

steps: Three days before eating, purchase the tripe from the best tripe shop and wash, clean, and scrape the tripe thoroughly.
Place the tripe in a basin and for twenty-four to thirty hours keep it under running water from a fountain spout so that the water in the basin remains fresh.

The day before eating, cut the tripe into squares smaller than chocolate ounces and boil in plenty of water in a large pot with garlic, carrots, onions with cloves embedded in them, salt, pepper, nutmeg, bay leaf, thyme, and rosemary.
Add four veal hands, a pair of chorizos, and one morcilla, and ensure the cooking, without being vigorous, is animated and even for eight consecutive hours, as any interruption will ruin the dish.
When the chorizo and morcilla are cooked, remove and reserve on a plate, then remove the veal hands, bone them carefully, and shred the meat.
Once the tripe is cooked, remove from the pot, draining well, and let cool in a basin or large dish for an entire night.
The next day, two and a half to three hours before eating, wash the tripe in hot water to eliminate the gelatinous and slimy coating covering it.
In a large saucepan over high heat, in three quarters of a pound of lard, sauté six onions and twelve cloves of garlic with three quarters of a pound of lean, well-cured ham cut into dice.
Season and add a few points of chili pepper, then add the chorizo and morcilla in small pieces.
When the onion takes color, sauté the tripe and veal hands, being careful that nothing sticks to the bottom of the pan, then quickly add good clean broth that covers the dish well.

As soon as everything begins to boil, place strips of fresh or preserved pimientos on top and put the tripe in the oven at medium heat for two hours, or if there is no oven, over very low heat on the stove for slow cooking.
Serve very hot and drink plenty of white wine.

title: Cardo con Tuétano (Cardoon with Marrow)
description: Prepared with pork or lard or oil, broth, and sauce.

ingredients.name: Broth from the pot, clean and defatted

steps: Kill the corners of the stalk and cut into pieces fifteen centimeters long.
Blanch the pieces in boiling water with a pinch of salt until the outer layer comes off easily.
Add cold water to the hot water to be able to put your hands in and manipulate the cardoon pieces, removing the skin and putting them in very cold water as they are peeled.
Remove and let drain very well to put them in a saucepan with a very loose roux-based sauce.
Wet with broth from the pot, clean and defatted, in quantity sufficient to cover all the cardoon, and cook over very low heat until all the sauce is consumed.
Place the cardoons in a serving dish, and pour over at the moment of serving a white sauce well bound with two or three egg yolks, dissolved in half a cup of water.

title: Carne de Membrillo (Quince Paste)
description: Prepared with quinces, water, and sugar.

ingredients.name: sugar in proportion of five pounds sugar to six pounds fruit

steps: Choose very ripe and yellow quinces and prepare them to heat the syrup afterwards, which should be in the proportion of six pounds of fruit to five pounds of sugar; peel the quinces and put them with sufficient quantity of water in a small cauldron, which should be on the fire so that the quinces do not turn black, and add them in pieces as they are peeled, in hot water, taking care that the boiling does not stop from when it begins, so that it does not take on the color of wine and is well yellow and pleasant to the sight

When the water does not cover them well, always add more, well heated and boiled, in no way cold; as soon as the pieces are well cooked and soft, but still whole, remove them with a skimmer and spread them on a clean cloth, and when cold, pound them well in a marble mortar or pass them through a fairly open strainer

Make a thick syrup of half a cuartilla of water per pound of sugar, and well clarified, pour into it—cold or hot, it makes no difference—the prepared quince paste, put it on the fire and stir until it takes the consistency of preserve; this is also poured while hot into glasses, jars or small tin boxes, and after four days have passed; if the open boxes are placed in an oven for half an hour, a thin film forms which preserves the sweet for a long time

title: Chocha a la Vizcaina (Woodcock Biscay Style)
description: Prepared with woodcock, pork, and bacon.
steps: After removing the entrails from the woodcock (which will be kept for the sauce) and arranging it so the beak comes out between the right breast, place it in a small pot with pork butter, a thin slice of bacon, two or three small onions, two cups of broth, a measure of Sherry, and four small turnips, being careful to move the pot from time to time and adding broth if it reduces.

When the woodcock has cooked enough, fry separately one very finely chopped onion, and when it is half done, add the chopped entrails of the woodcock to the same pan so they release all their juice, but being careful to first remove the crop or pouch, which gives a bad taste. Add a little flour and all the sauce together.

title: Chocha Asada (Roasted Woodcock)
description: Prepared with woodcock, bacon, and beef.
steps: Pluck and singe the woodcock.
Clean and truss it, passing the beak through the body.
Remove the giblets by opening along the back and extracting the intestines.
Mince the giblets and mix with 60 grams of beef lard and trimmed truffles.
Stuff the woodcock body with this mixture.
Cover the woodcock with thin bacon leaves, securing them with twine according to the illustration.
Roast over gentle, even, and prolonged heat so that the abundant meat of the bird cooks through well.
Remove the bacon and twine at the moment of serving.
Serve with fried croutons soaked in the juices and plenty of watercress on the platter.

title: Choucroute (Fermented Cabbage)
description: Prepared with bacon, chorizo, and pork.

ingredients.name: 1 pound of smoked bacon, finely sliced
1 sobreasada or chorizo weighing half a pound
half a cuartillo of white wine

steps: Desalt the choucroute by soaking in water for three hours. Drain well and press it with two casserole lids.
Place the choucroute in a casserole over gentle heat with 1 pound of smoked bacon cut into very fine slices, 1 sobreasada or chorizo weighing half a pound, and 125 grams of pork lard.
Moisten with half a cuartillo of white wine and 2 ladles of good clean broth. Season carefully with salt and pepper and add a pinch of grated nutmeg.
Cook the cabbage with the bacon and chorizo for five consecutive hours over very low heat.

When serving, cut the sausage into slices and arrange them on the platter with symmetry. If the broth is abundant, reduce it over a lively fire while arranging the dish, but without adding anything else.

title: Chuleta de Vaca a la Milanesa (Beef Chop Milanese Style)
description: Prepared with beef, broth, and white wine or sherry.

ingredients.name: one beef chop, prepared and larded
one quarter liter of white wine or Sherry
three hours cooking time over low heat
grated Parmesan cheese, or equal parts Gruyère and Manchego cheese

steps: Cook one beef chop, prepared and larded but slightly more seasoned, in one quarter liter of broth mixed with one quarter liter of white wine or Sherry
After three hours of cooking over low heat, remove the pan from the heat
Pass the juice through a sieve and reduce by half
Separately, cook macaroni in broth from the stew pot and sprinkle generously with grated Parmesan cheese, or if not available, equal parts Gruyère and Manchego cheese
Place the macaroni on a serving platter and place the chop on top
Pour the reduced cooking juice over everything

title: Chuleta de Vaca a lo Hortera (Beef Chop Hortera Style)
description: Prepared with beef, broth, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one beef chop, prepared and larded
a bouquet of parsley and scallions
one head of red cabbage, cut into slices

steps: Prepare and lard the chop as previously described
Cook over low heat for one hour in one liter of broth with 125 grams of fresh bacon
Add a bouquet of parsley and scallions, six carrots, one bay leaf, two onions with cloves, and one head of red cabbage cut into slices
Let cook two hours more
Remove the meat, take off the twine, and place on a large serving platter
Arrange the cabbage and carrots around it
If the broth is thin, reduce it over high heat before pouring it over the dish
